scenes.tts: Why does a week of closure rewire a kitten's cortex, while months do nothing visible in an adult?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Window and the Patch. A kitten and an adult cat, each with one eye closed. Convention: left hemisphere recorded; right eye (contralateral) orange, left eye (ipsilateral) blue; histograms run group 1 on the left to group 7 on the right.
scenes.narration: Why does a week of closure rewire a kitten's cortex, while months do nothing visible in an adult?

scenes.tts: Every result so far depends on age. Two terms help.
scenes.visual: Two empty boxes, one nested inside the other.
scenes.narration: Every result so far depends on age. Two terms help.

scenes.tts: A sensitive period is a window in which experience has an unusually strong effect.
scenes.visual: Outer box fills: sensitive period, experience has an unusually strong effect.
scenes.narration: A sensitive period is a window in which experience has an unusually strong effect.

scenes.tts: A critical period, in Eric Knudsen's definition, is a sensitive period with two extra features.
scenes.visual: Inner box labelled critical period. Credit: Knudsen's definition.
scenes.narration: A critical period, in Eric Knudsen's definition, is a sensitive period with two extra features.

scenes.tts: The experience is essential for normal development. And its effects last.
scenes.visual: Inner box adds two lines: essential for normal development; effects last.
scenes.narration: The experience is essential for normal development. And its effects last.

scenes.tts: Real windows often fall between the two. How sharp one looks depends on the species, the manipulation and the measure.
scenes.visual: Three dials labelled species, manipulation, measure.
scenes.narration: Real windows often fall between the two. How sharp one looks depends on the species, the manipulation and the measure.

scenes.tts: An adult cat's histogram may not move after a closure. That does not mean the adult cortex cannot change at all.
scenes.visual: An unchanged adult histogram, with a note: not the same as no change of any kind.
scenes.narration: An adult cat's histogram may not move after a closure. That does not mean the adult cortex cannot change at all.

scenes.tts: Name the species with every number, because the window differs.
scenes.visual: Three timelines stack up, each labelled with a species.
scenes.narration: Name the species with every number, because the window differs.

scenes.tts: In kittens, susceptibility begins around the start of the fourth week. It stays high to about six to eight weeks, then declines through the third month.
scenes.visual: Kitten timeline: rise at week 4, high to about weeks 6 to 8, decline through month 3.
scenes.narration: In kittens, susceptibility begins around the start of the fourth week. It stays high to about six to eight weeks, then declines through the third month.

scenes.tts: In macaques, early closure has its strongest effect in the first weeks after birth.
scenes.visual: Macaque timeline: strongest in the first weeks after birth.
scenes.narration: In macaques, early closure has its strongest effect in the first weeks after birth.

scenes.tts: In mice, Joshua Gordon and Michael Stryker found the strongest shifts near postnatal day twenty-eight.
scenes.caption: In mice, Joshua Gordon and Michael Stryker found the strongest shifts near postnatal day 28.
scenes.visual: Mouse timeline: peak near P28. Credit: Gordon and Stryker, 1996.
scenes.narration: In mice, Joshua Gordon and Michael Stryker found the strongest shifts near postnatal day 28.

scenes.tts: The same few days of closure in adult mice did little.
scenes.visual: Mouse timeline: adult segment flat.
scenes.narration: The same few days of closure in adult mice did little.

scenes.tts: Mice have no ocular dominance columns. Their value is genetics, used to ask what opens and closes the window.
scenes.visual: A mouse cortex with a small binocular zone and no stripes; a DNA icon beside it.
scenes.narration: Mice have no ocular dominance columns. Their value is genetics, used to ask what opens and closes the window.

scenes.tts: Now the clinic. Amblyopia is reduced vision, usually in one eye, that glasses do not immediately restore.
scenes.visual: A child with glasses; one eye's view stays blurred. Label: amblyopia.
scenes.narration: Now the clinic. Amblyopia is reduced vision, usually in one eye, that glasses do not immediately restore.

scenes.tts: No structural disease of the eye explains it.
scenes.visual: The weak eye drawn healthy in structure.
scenes.narration: No structural disease of the eye explains it.

scenes.tts: It usually arises when the two eyes give the young brain unequal input.
scenes.visual: Two input arrows into a young brain, one thick and one thin.
scenes.narration: It usually arises when the two eyes give the young brain unequal input.

scenes.tts: Common causes are strabismus, a large difference in focus between the eyes, and anything that blocks one eye's image.
scenes.visual: Three icons: a turned eye, two lenses of very different strength, a clouded lens and a drooping lid.
scenes.narration: Common causes are strabismus, a large difference in focus between the eyes, and anything that blocks one eye's image.

scenes.tts: Strabismus affects a few percent of children.
scenes.visual: Label: strabismus, a few percent of children.
scenes.narration: Strabismus affects a few percent of children.

scenes.tts: Predict. A young child's left eye sees poorly after early strabismus. Glasses correct the optics. Which eye do you patch?
scenes.visual: Question card: which eye do you patch? A child with a turned left eye wearing glasses.
scenes.narration: Predict. A young child's left eye sees poorly after early strabismus. Glasses correct the optics. Which eye do you patch?

scenes.tts: The good eye. A patch covers it for part of the day, or atropine drops blur it.
scenes.visual: A patch goes over the right eye; an alternative panel shows atropine drops blurring it.
scenes.narration: The good eye. A patch covers it for part of the day, or atropine drops blur it.

scenes.tts: Then the weak eye carries the useful visual input.
scenes.visual: The left eye's input arrow thickens.
scenes.narration: Then the weak eye carries the useful visual input.

scenes.tts: For those hours the weak eye is the one helping the shared cells fire, so the contest tilts its way.
scenes.visual: Rule card returns: the cell keeps the eye that helps it fire. The weak eye's bars on the histogram regrow.
scenes.narration: For those hours the weak eye is the one helping the shared cells fire, so the contest tilts its way.

scenes.tts: That can work because the weak eye keeps pathways that can still be strengthened, even if some connections were lost.
scenes.visual: The weak eye's remaining synapses drawn thin but present, then thickening; one lost branch stays gone.
scenes.narration: That can work because the weak eye keeps pathways that can still be strengthened, even if some connections were lost.

scenes.tts: Treatment generally works best in young children, consistent with a sensitive period. Trials have found some older children still improve.
scenes.visual: A bar for young children tall; a bar for older children shorter but above zero. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Treatment generally works best in young children, consistent with a sensitive period. Trials have found some older children still improve.

scenes.tts: A cataract that blocks one eye from birth is usually removed early in infancy, for the same reason.
scenes.visual: An infant's clouded lens is cleared early.
scenes.narration: A cataract that blocks one eye from birth is usually removed early in infancy, for the same reason.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: the cell keeps the eye that helps it fire. That contest counts most while the window is open.
scenes.visual: Closing card: the rule, and an open window.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: the cell keeps the eye that helps it fire. That contest counts most while the window is open.

scenes.tts: What opens and closes that window is the next lesson's question.
scenes.visual: A window frame half closed, labelled: next lesson.
scenes.narration: What opens and closes that window is the next lesson's question.
